title: Supramolecular Porous Assemblies of Atomically Precise Catalytically Active Cerium-Based Clusters

material_class.structural_family: Benzoate-capped cerium oxo cluster in a supramolecular porous assembly

synthesis.procedure: Benzoic acid (500 mg, 4 mmol) was dissolved in N,N-diethylformamide (5 mL) by sonication in an 8-dram vial. Ce6 glycine-cluster precursor (120 mg, 0.05 mmol) and water (2.5 mL) were added, followed by further sonication. The vial was heated at 120 °C for 18 h and cooled to room temperature. The tan-brown product was centrifuged, washed with N,N-diethylformamide, acetone, and ethanol, soaked in ethanol overnight, and dried under vacuum.
synthesis.temperature: 120 °C for reaction; 80 °C and then 30 °C for drying
synthesis.time: 18 h reaction; 30 min at 80 °C and 18 h at 30 °C during drying
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Centrifuged for 5 min; washed twice each with N,N-diethylformamide (10 mL) and acetone (10 mL), then twice with ethanol (10 mL), with 20 min soaking before centrifugation. Soaked in ethanol overnight, washed twice more with ethanol, dried in a vacuum oven for 30 min at 80 °C, then under high vacuum for 18 h at 30 °C.

properties.summary: Continuous-wave EPR detected a signal attributed to an S = 1/2 species, presumed to be Ce(III); this supported the mixed valency indicated by XPS. No bulk magnetic or optical-property measurement was reported.

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: The discrete Ce38 core has a 4:9:12:9:4 cerium-layering motif. Sixteen benzoate ligands cap the cluster; interactions between phenyl rings of neighboring clusters organize it into a porous supramolecular lattice.

material_class.structural_family: 2-Naphthoate-capped cerium oxo cluster in a supramolecular porous assembly

synthesis.procedure: 2-Naphthoic acid (700 mg, 4 mmol) was dissolved in N,N-diethylformamide (5 mL) by sonication in an 8-dram vial. Ce6 glycine-cluster precursor (120 mg; the article prints 4 mmol) and water (2.5 mL) were added, followed by further sonication. The vial was heated at 120 °C for 18 h and cooled to room temperature. The yellow-orange product was centrifuged, washed with N,N-diethylformamide, acetone, and ethanol, soaked in ethanol overnight, and dried under vacuum.
